title: Absolute confidentiality conflicts with reporting
impact: Users may be told privacy is absolute while the system still reports aggregated analysis.
recommendation: Separate personal confidentiality from aggregated reporting and legal exceptions.
contract: Privacy contract: what is private, what is aggregated, who can access it, and legal exceptions.
clarification_contract: Do not state privacy as absolute until the access, aggregation, reporting, and exception rules are explicit.
clarifying_questions: Who can see individual messages?
Are reports aggregated only?
What are the legal exception cases?
fix_draft: Conversations are private at the individual level unless legally required; aggregated, non-identifying insights may be reported to management.

title: Harassment or violence is treated as a generic forbidden topic
impact: The assistant may become passive when the user needs urgent human support.
recommendation: Create a dedicated safety escalation contract for harassment, violence, and self-harm signals.
contract: Safety escalation contract: acknowledge seriousness, avoid investigation, direct to HR/security/emergency resources.
clarification_contract: Do not treat urgent user harm as a normal refusal. First define the approved escalation path and wording.
clarifying_questions: Which human team should receive urgent safety cases?
Should the bot provide emergency resources?
What exact wording is approved for escalation?
fix_draft: If the user reports harassment, violence, or immediate risk, acknowledge the seriousness and direct them to HR or emergency support without giving legal or investigative advice.

title: Smalltalk role appears to collect HR signals
impact: The agent boundary is blurred; casual chat may silently become assessment.
recommendation: Declare when smalltalk can hand off to interview flow and what it must not infer.
contract: Agent boundary contract: role, allowed topics, handoff trigger, forbidden inference.
clarification_contract: Do not let a casual agent silently perform assessment. Define whether it collects, hands off, or only responds socially.
clarifying_questions: Can smalltalk collect HR signals or only hand off?
What triggers interviewer handoff?
What must smalltalk never score or infer?
fix_draft: Smalltalk may respond socially and may suggest a handoff when work wellbeing appears relevant, but it must not score or probe HR categories itself.

title: Function-call requirement lacks a strict schema
impact: Routing output may be malformed or inconsistent across model providers.
recommendation: Define a provider-neutral function schema with required fields and enum values.
contract: Tool contract: name, required args, enum values, payload shape, invalid-state behavior.
clarification_contract: Do not rely on natural-language tool calls. Define exact schema, required fields, enums, and invalid-state behavior.
clarifying_questions: What are the exact enum values?
Which fields are required?
What should happen if routing confidence is low?
fix_draft: Define route_to_agent(agent_to_dispatch enum, conversation_phase enum, next_action_directive string, payload object) and reject free-form output.

title: Output format is underspecified
impact: The same prompt can produce different shapes, which breaks parsing and evaluation.
recommendation: Add explicit output format, length, and failure behavior.
contract: Output contract: structure, max length, language, refusal shape, examples.
clarification_contract: Do not return free-form output. First determine format, length, language, and insufficient-data behavior.
clarifying_questions: What output format do you need?
What is the max length?
What should the model do when data is insufficient?
fix_draft: Return only the requested structure. Include max length, language, and a fallback response when inputs are insufficient.

title: Long prompt lacks section tags
impact: Long unstructured prompts are harder to audit, patch, and test.
recommendation: Split into named sections such as role, boundaries, memory, safety, output, examples.
contract: Maintainability contract: stable section tags and single source of truth for repeated policies.
clarification_contract: Do not patch long prompt text blindly. First identify authoritative sections and repeated policies.
clarifying_questions: Which sections are authoritative?
Can repeated policies be centralized?
Which examples are normative vs illustrative?

title: User asks for a deliverable without an output contract
impact: The model will likely produce a plausible generic answer while the user expects a specific structure, scope, or evidence standard.
recommendation: Ask for or define the deliverable contract before generation.
contract: Deliverable contract: audience, scope, sections, evidence, length, output format, and success criteria.
clarification_contract: Do not produce the deliverable yet. First collect missing decision points for scope, data, audience, format, and success criteria.
clarifying_questions: Which data should the report use?
What date range matters?
Who is the audience?
Which sections and format do you want?
What extra context or files should be included?
fix_draft: Before answering, define: target audience, exact scope, required sections, evidence standard, output format, and max length.

title: Later exception may override an earlier hard boundary
impact: The model may follow the later exception and weaken the earlier boundary, especially in long prompts.
recommendation: Convert boundaries into ordered precedence rules with explicit exceptions.
contract: Precedence contract: highest priority rules, allowed exceptions, and what happens when rules conflict.
clarification_contract: Do not decide silently which instruction wins. Ask for rule priority, allowed exceptions, and conflict behavior.
clarifying_questions: Which rule has priority?
Are there allowed exceptions?
What should happen when two rules conflict?
fix_draft: Add a precedence section: Safety > privacy > tool schema > task style. Exceptions must not override higher-priority boundaries.

title: Long context is provided without a state retention contract
impact: The model may not reliably remember or prioritize the intended parts of the long context across turns.
recommendation: Define which context must be retained, ignored, summarized, or refreshed.
contract: State contract: durable facts, ephemeral context, relevance rule, summarization rule, truncation behavior.
clarification_contract: Do not assume long context will be remembered or prioritized. Define durable state, relevance, and summarization behavior.
clarifying_questions: Which facts must persist?
Which history should be ignored?
When should old context be summarized?
What is the truncation rule?
fix_draft: Add a state section: keep only durable user facts and the latest relevant turn; summarize older context; ignore irrelevant history.

title: Prompt asks the model to know facts without an uncertainty contract
impact: The model may answer as if it has reliable knowledge even when the prompt lacks source data.
recommendation: Add uncertainty, source, and refusal behavior.
contract: Uncertainty contract: source of truth, confidence threshold, unknown response, and escalation path.
clarification_contract: Do not answer with certainty until source data, confidence threshold, and unknown response are defined.
clarifying_questions: What is the source of truth?
What should the model say if the data is missing?
Should it ask for sources or escalate?
fix_draft: If required facts are not present in the provided context or trusted source, say that the information is unavailable instead of guessing.

title: Task command is too broad to execute reliably
impact: The model may pick an arbitrary interpretation and complete the wrong task while appearing successful.
recommendation: Ask for the missing execution contract before taking irreversible or broad action.
contract: Execution contract: exact target, scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, verification method, and stopping condition.
clarification_contract: Do not execute the task yet if target, scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria are missing.
approval_contract: Approve only when target, scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, verification command, and stopping condition are explicit.
clarifying_questions: What exact target should be changed?
What is in scope and out of scope?
How should success be verified?
Are there files, examples, or constraints to use?
fix_draft: Before executing, define target, scope, constraints, acceptance criteria, verification command, and stopping condition.

title: Coding prompt asks for output without assigning responsibility
impact: The model may act like a code generator instead of an accountable engineer, causing vague scope, weak verification, and unreviewable output.
recommendation: Assign responsibility, boundaries, constraints, architecture expectations, verification, and final accountability output.
contract: Responsibility contract: role, owned surface, constraints, non-goals, architecture expectations, verification, changed-files report, residual risk.
clarification_contract: Do not ask only for code. First assign who the model is responsible as, what surface it owns, what it must preserve, how it verifies success, and what it must report back.
approval_contract: Approve only when the prompt names role/responsibility, owned files or module, constraints/non-goals, verification, and final report format.
clarifying_questions: What role/responsibility should the model assume?
Which module or files does it own?
What behavior must be preserved?
How should it verify success?
What should the final engineering report include?
fix_draft: Act as a senior engineer responsible for <owned surface>. Implement <task> while preserving <constraints/non-goals>. Verify with <tests/commands>. Return changed files, root cause/design rationale, verification results, and residual risks.

title: Technical change lacks risk and verification contract
impact: The model may implement a risky technical change without rollback, compatibility, validation, or verification guarantees.
recommendation: Require a technical risk contract before implementation.
contract: Technical risk contract: target surface, compatibility/rollback, validation/error model, security/performance risks, verification command.
clarification_contract: Do not implement yet. First identify the technical surface, risk controls, rollback/compatibility needs, and verification method.
approval_contract: Approve only when target surface, risk controls, rollback/compatibility, validation/error model, and verification are explicit.
clarifying_questions: What exact technical surface is changing?
What compatibility or rollback rule applies?
What validation/error/security risks matter?
How should this be tested?
What behavior must remain unchanged?
fix_draft: Before implementing, define the target files/routes/schema, compatibility and rollback rules, validation/error handling, security/performance risks, and verification command.

title: Recommendation prompt lacks decision context
impact: The model may invent a generic recommendation that does not fit the user's location, budget, preferences, timing, or constraints.
recommendation: Ask for the missing decision context before recommending.
contract: Recommendation contract: location/market, budget, preferences, constraints, timing, and decision criteria.
clarification_contract: Do not recommend yet. First collect the decision context that changes the correct answer.
approval_contract: Approve only when location/market, budget, preferences, constraints, and timing are explicit or intentionally defaulted.
clarifying_questions: Where should this apply?
What budget or price range matters?
What preferences or use case should drive the choice?
When is this needed?
Any constraints, allergies, or must-avoid options?
fix_draft: Before recommending, ask for location/market, budget, preferences, timing, constraints, and ranking criteria; if the user wants defaults, state assumptions clearly.

title: High-stakes personal advice lacks safety and source contract
impact: The model may give medical, financial, legal, or other high-stakes advice without enough user context or professional boundaries.
recommendation: Add a high-stakes safety contract: ask for context, avoid guarantees, cite source limits, and escalate to professionals where appropriate.
contract: High-stakes advice contract: domain boundary, user context, risk factors, source of truth, uncertainty behavior, professional escalation.
clarification_contract: Do not provide direct advice yet. First collect risk-relevant context and define professional/escalation boundaries.
approval_contract: Approve only when source limits, uncertainty behavior, and professional escalation are explicit.
clarifying_questions: What relevant context changes the answer?
Are there risk factors or constraints?
What source of truth should be used?
Should this be framed as general information, not professional advice?
When should the user contact a professional?
fix_draft: For high-stakes topics, provide general information only, ask for risk-relevant context, avoid guarantees, and direct the user to a qualified professional for decisions.
